newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower on Hanbo Steel trouble.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower on Hanbo Steel trouble.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed lower on Thursday after a day of fluctuations as media reports on financial trouble at Hanbo Steel dented buying sentiment, brokers said.
"Hanbo's trouble helped wipe out early gains from a technical rebound," said Yoo Jae-kyong of Daishin Securities.
The composite stock index shed 2.03 points to close at a provisional 676.91.
Hanbo officials said the group chairman and his relatives would hand over their stake in the ill-fated steel company to creditor banks.
Creditor banks said a takeover was sought for Hanbo as its debt snowballed as a result of excessive facility expansion.
"Given the size of the 5.5 trillion won debt, settlement is not going to be easy," said Kim Nam-soo, an analyst at Hyundai Securities.
Bank officials said fresh loans could be pumped into the troubled Hanbo to help finish construction of a steel mill in the southeastern city of Tangjin.
Analysts said the construction has so far cost 4.96 trillion won and an additional 750 billion won would be needed for completion. Hanbo Steel fell 370 won to 5,390.
Brokers said the yen's fall against the dollar raised concern over export recovery.
They feared the yen's weakness would make South Korean exports less competitive against Japanese products.
Prospects that the row over a controversial labour law would drag on dampened overall sentiment, brokers said.
Falling customer deposits with securities houses and rising interest rates were also blamed for the fall.
Volume totalled 31.04 million shares, compared with 36.68 million on Wednesday. Losers outpaced gainers 464 to 322 with 120 unchanged. -- KIM MYONG-HWAN (822) 727 5645
